title: Apple-Cinnamon Pancakes
changes_from_base: The same buttermilk and soured cream batter, but each pancake is scattered with cinnamon-sugared chopped apple before it is flipped.
summary: Warm, spiced pancakes studded with fresh apple, cinnamon-sweet, tender and quick to come together.
equipment: nonstick frying pan (30 cm) or griddle
wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
unsalted butter, melted and cooled slightly
apples, peeled, cored and finely chopped

steps.title: Prepare oven and mix dry
steps.text: Heat oven to 93 °C; spray a wire rack and put it in the oven on its tray. Whisk 283 g plain flour, 2 tbsp caster sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, ½ tsp bicarbonate of soda and ½ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Mix wet
steps.text: Whisk 480 ml buttermilk, 2 large eggs, 60 ml soured cream and 42 g unsalted butter (melted and cooled slightly), pour into a well in the flour and stir gently until just combined (lumpy); rest 10 min.

steps.title: Prepare topping
steps.text: Mix 2 apples (peeled, cored and finely chopped), 1 tbsp light brown sugar and ½ tsp ground cinnamon.

steps.title: Heat pan
steps.text: Heat 1 tsp vegetable oil in a 30 cm non-stick frying pan over medium heat until shimmering and wipe out the excess, leaving a thin film.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Cook 4 pancakes of 60 ml each until the edges are set, the base is golden and bubbles begin to break (2-3 min); sprinkle each with 1 tbsp apple mixture. Flip and cook 1-2 min more. Serve straight away or keep warm on the rack; repeat, adding the remaining oil as needed.

tips: Finely chop the apples rather than grating them; the pieces stay distinct and add pleasant pockets of texture.
Sprinkle the apple mixture on top of the pancake just before flipping; this prevents it soaking into the raw batter and keeps the pieces visible.
The thin film of oil left in the pan (rather than wiping it clean completely) ensures an even golden crust.
storage: Best served fresh and warm. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
